answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a stake-backed challenge assigned by a public beacon. At random intervals, it pairs each identity with peers outside its local cluster, requiring signed commitments and fresh answers tied to prior work. A fake identity cannot simply wander through a canyon of colluding accounts, because outside peers expose duplicated or inconsistent responses; the protocol then slashes its bond. Every extra identity therefore requires locked capital and creates another target for costly failure.
